solution: The variable $x$ is in the denominator, and division by $0$ is undefined, so there is a restriction: $x\neq 0$.
Multiply both sides of the equation by $x$ to clear the denominator: $\begin{aligned}\frac{{=a}}{x}&={=b}\\{=a}&={=b}x\end{aligned}$

Check the answer by substituting $x={=s}$ back into the original equation: $\begin{aligned}\text{LHS}&=\frac{{=a}}{{=s}}\\&={=a // s}\\&=\text{RHS}\end{aligned}$ Both sides are equal, and ${=s}\neq 0$, so the restriction is respected and $x={=s}$ is the solution.
notes: Entry-point skill: the variable is alone in one denominator and the right-hand side is a whole number, so the only moves are state x != 0, multiply both sides by x, divide by the coefficient, and check by substitution. It is the simplest case of the book's ex4-1-15 (4/p = 16/24, page 78, which cross-multiplies) and its solution follows the four steps of worked example 2 (restriction, multiply, solve, check by substitution). Parameters: the answer s is drawn first (2 to 12) and the right-hand side b (2 to 9), so a = b*s is always exactly divisible and the answer is always a positive whole number (largest numerator 108). That gives 88 distinct (a, b) stems; the same numerator can recur but never with the same b and a different answer. The restriction is x != 0 for every instance and the answer is never 0, so no instance has an extraneous root. No distractors, so no misconception ids are attached; the catalogued misconception about the restriction seeming optional is addressed by the worked solution stating it in step 1 and re-checking it in step 4. The multiplies-only-the-fractions misconception cannot arise because there is no term without a denominator on the left. Standard and advanced tiers were not listed as gaps and are already covered by the book's own questions (ex4-1-25, ex4-1-27 standard; ex4-1-23, ex4-7-2g advanced), so no further families were written.
